s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic papular eruption of the extremities with a chronic time course
salient_findings: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on the extremities
Erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
3-month history of symptoms
No remarkable medical or family history
No concurrent medications
Previous treatment with topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets had no effect
Palms, soles, and oral mucosa not involved
Normal laboratory tests, including blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor
Skin biopsy showed mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

per_call: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren's syndrome

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of pruritic papules on the extremities with histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis

shortlist.label: Grover disease
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by pruritic papules on the extremities, consistent with the patient's symptoms and histopathological findings of individual cell dyskeratosis and vacuolar degeneration of the basal cell layer

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with chronic, pruritic papules, and the histopathological findings of mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Nummular dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with pruritic papules on the extremities, and the patient's history of ineffective treatment with topical steroid ointments is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause pruritic papules, and the histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including intensively pruritic papules and the presence of individual cell dyskeratosis and vacuolar degeneration of the basal cell layer in the skin biopsy, are consistent with Grover disease. The lack of response to topical steroid ointments and oral compound glycyrrhizin tablets also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: The absence of palm and sole involvement and the lack of characteristic orange-red scaling make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathology do not match the typical findings of this condition, which often includes more pronounced lymphocytic infiltrate and epidermal changes

rejected.label: Nummular dermatitis
rejected.why: The distribution and morphology of the lesions, as well as the histopathological findings, do not align with nummular dermatitis

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings, such as the presence of individual cell dyskeratosis and vacuolar degeneration, are not typical of lichen planus
